leads.name: Northfield churchyard yew (St Laurence)
leads.reason: One source only (Ancient Yew Group tree 7124, 'Notable', girth 400 cm at 1 m, taken from Street View and unverified, earliest mention a 1921 photograph). No age basis, no photo, no coordinate beyond churchyard grid ref SP0255079342. Churchyard public. Could ship as approximate with location_site if a second source or a Geograph photo of the yew turns up. Recheck 2026-11-19: northfield-uk.blogspot.com 2015 church post returned an empty shell to curl; no second source for the yew (search found none); still one source.
leads.how_to_recognise: A twisted yew at the top of the steps leading into St Laurence church (AYG Street View note).

leads.name: Cofton Hackett fallen yew (St Michael and All Angels)
leads.city: Birmingham (day trip, Cofton Hackett, Worcestershire; transport time not verified)
leads.reason: AYG class 'Ancient', girth 5-7 m, fallen male yew SW of the 14th-century church, visited 2002 (Tim Hills); 'reputed more than 800 years old' per a 1946 rector quote relayed by AYG text on a blog mirror. One source, last visit 2002, not alive-checked, outside the city, 30-minute public transport not confirmed.
leads.how_to_recognise: Fallen, horse-shoe shaped yew lying SW of the church, per AYG.

leads.name: Highbury Park yew (Moseley)
leads.reason: Only a local blog (coppicing.blogspot.com/2016/02/the-yew.html) mentions a single yew of significant age near the old Highbury estate quadrangle of yews; no age, girth, coordinate or register. Blog is not a source.

leads.name: Acocks Green Oak (Arden Road, B27)
leads.reason: Street oak standing in the road; only a paywalled Substack post (2023) and a search summary; no age, girth or coordinate seen on a fetched page.

leads.name: Birmingham Botanical Gardens copper beech
leads.reason: Owner's own pages (fetched 2026-11-18): 'older than the Gardens' (opened 1832), on maps from Holly Bank Farm days, 'our 200-year-old treasure', mulched and protected in 2025 (alive), near the main lawn. Paid entry (day ticket). No tree-level coordinate (lat/lon is the garden's, approximate), a walk-through garden so no location_site allowed, no photo. Becomes shippable with an OSM node, a geotagged photo or a reader's GPS fix at the beech. Pass 2026-11-19 (7th): the Gardens say they hold 7 Tree Register national champion trees and 32 locally significant specimens, listed in birmingham.gardenexplorer.org tour 'Champion Trees' (#12); that site is an ASP.NET app, tour.aspx?id=12 and a viewstate postback both returned an empty tour list to curl, so the named champions and their coordinates were not read. A session with a rendering browser could open that tour and the per-specimen map points. Pass 2026-11-20 (8th): tried the ASP.NET postback with the tour selected and a direct POST to tour.aspx/GetFeatures (returns {"d":null} without session state); still no champion list. Highbury Park 2018 survey PDF is image-only (no text layer; WebFetch and a raw stream read both failed), so the 515 cm oak stays unverified. Wikidata individual-tree (Q811534) query within 20 km of central Birmingham returned 0 items.

leads.reason: Express and Star (page 403s, search summary only) says a c. 250-year-old oak on council land at Mills Avenue is protected and a resident fought a felling plan. Nothing seen on a fetched page, outcome unknown, no coordinate.

leads.name: Sutton Park veteran oak (ATI 249969)
leads.reason: Woodland Trust Ancient Tree Inventory (fetched 2026-11-18): veteran, standing, girth 3.95 m at 1.5 m, decaying wood, holly crowding it, grid ref SP1093796185 (about 52.57N, 1.84W, not converted or checked). Recorded by a volunteer 2023, last visited 2024. No age, no photo, a nameless oak in a 900-hectare walk-through park so no location_site; modest girth. One source, approximate at best; not worth a page alone.

leads.name: Solihull bowling green yew (Ramada/George Hotel, near St Alphege)
leads.reason: Ancient Yew Group 'Notable', tree 1204, access 'Public' but it is in a hotel's bowling green; no girth, no grid ref ('not known'), one source. Access unclear.

leads.name: Grove Park cedar, Harborne
leads.reason: Council park (Grove Park, Harborne Park Road, B17 0BJ, free). normanfield.com (fetched 2026-11-18, local history page) calls it the ancient centre-piece of The Grove and says it is thought planted about 1785 by Thomas Green; The Street Tree substack (paywalled, 403, search summary only) says it may have been planted by Thomas Attwood (lived there 1823 to 1846) and calls it one of Birmingham finest cedars. Planter conflict, no girth, no register, no tree-level coordinate, no Commons photo; lifecheck NONE. Park is not a small site. Needs a GPS fix or photograph to ship.

leads.name: Highbury Park biggest veteran oak (515 cm)
leads.reason: Friends of Highbury Park veteran survey (2018 leaflet, PDF unreadable; figure seen only in search summaries and Grokipedia): 38 veterans over 3 m, largest an oak at 515 cm, beech 420 cm. Survey table at highburyparkfriends.org.uk/database/trees/hpftreesurvey.php is dead (returns 0 rows). No location, no figure seen on a fetched page. Council park, open. Needs the Friends survey table or a GPS fix.

leads.name: Sutton Park holly coppice stool, Holly Hurst edge (ATI 268643)
leads.reason: Woodland Trust Ancient Tree Inventory page fetched 2026-11-19: veteran, standing, alive, coppice stool girth 7.17 m at 0.15 m, GPS, surveyed and verified Nov 2024 by one recorder, public open access beside a footpath outside Holly Hurst. Single source (ATI), a coppice stool not a collectible trunk, no photograph in reach; not shipped.

Single source, last survey 2015, a field in Warwickshire outside Birmingham; no web mention of the name found. Needs a second source or a reader GPS fix.
